today.name: shim-cli
today.tagline: See what your coding agent sends. Mask what you can.
today.description: An open-source hook and local proxy for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and VS Code. In Claude Code it masks secrets and personal data in tool results before the model reads them, and shim watch shows what a session sent and cost. No account, no telemetry.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I'm Mertcan, one of the makers of shim-cli.We built it because we wanted to see what our own coding agents send to the model. A request carries a lot more than your prompt: the system prompt and the tools array, plus every file the agent read along the way. When the agent opens a .env, the keys in it go to the model too, and nothing in the session tells you.shim-cli sits next to the agent you already use and runs on your machine:• shim install claude adds hooks to Claude Code. When a tool result holds an API key, a password, an email, an IBAN, a phone number or a Turkish ID number, the model gets a placeholder like <SECRET_1> instead.• shim watch -- claude runs one session through a local proxy and prints where the input tokens went, what the session cost (or would cost on an API key), and which sensitive values were in the request and the response. It forwards every byte unchanged.There's no account and no telemetry, and the hook adds no network destination. Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code are supported too, with less coverage.What it cannot do, so you know before you install:• A prompt you type into Claude Code or Codex is not masked, because neither client lets a hook rewrite it. shim reports it, or stops it under enforce. Copilot CLI does get the masked prompt.• In Claude Code, shell commands, the output of a failed command and files attached with @ are reported, not masked.• Codex and Copilot CLI tool traffic is not inspected, and VS Code only reports.• Detection is best effort and misses some values. It is not a DLP boundary.• macOS and Linux only. Windows is first on our list.Try it in a minute:uv tool install --python 3.12 shimshim demo claudeshim install claudeIt's Apache-2.0 on GitHub. The feedback we want most: what shim missed in your own sessions, and which client we should go deeper on next.

I build everything with Claude Code without being a developer, so I honestly have no idea what goes out in each session. The shim watch cost view is what got me. Does it also make sense on a subscription plan, or is it mostly for people paying per API call?

When a tool result gets <SECRET_1> instead of the key and the agent then writes that placeholder into a config file or a curl call, does shim swap the real value back on the way out, or does the agent just end up with a broken file?

Coding agents today are reading files, executing commands, and sending all of that information to a model on every step, and in most cases, not many people know what left the machine. This is a new channel of data collection in the development process, and it's barely studied right now.From my point of view, working at GTM at shim, it's a small niche, but a vital one. It should be a default layer in your stack, like secret scanning and network logging. It will not be a magic solution, but a minimum for every team to enable without creating an account or going through the procurement cycle.

comments.text: We're launching 3AM today: an AI on-call engineer for the systems you can't rewrite. Three things shaped it:Engineers needed proof, not a guess. When it can't prove one, it says so and hands over what it found.Regulated teams needed it to stay inside. Banks, insurers and telcos can't send production data to someone else's cloud, and their regulators ask where every byte goes. So 3AM runs inside your network with no inbound ports, works fully air-gapped too, and the only thing that ever reaches us is a signed licence check. Literally.Everyone needed to stay in charge. Nobody wants an AI changing production on its own in the middle of the night. So every fix is rehearsed with a dry run first, then waits for a person's approval in Slack, Symphony, PagerDuty, xMatters or email (you name it). 3AM starts in shadow mode: it watches, proposes fixes and changes nothing. Giving it more autonomy takes two approvers. And every step goes on a hash-chained audit log your auditors can verify.Proof is the point. We test 3AM by breaking a real open-source core banking system, 244,000 lines of ten-year-old Java, on purpose, in 67 different ways. Every number we publish comes from those runs, and zero harmful actions is a release gate, not a target.If you or your team is fed up of prod being down at night (or even during the day), 3AM is for you!🎁 As a bonus, the first 90 days are on us! Try it, tell us where it falls short, and we'll fix it.Note that 3AM is AI, and in its open alpha stage. yesterday.name: Unfenced
yesterday.tagline: Land for sale that actually borders public land

week.description: Jockey is the first AI that understands your entire media library across photos and video. comments.text: We're launching the general availability of Jockey today, and it's shaped by what we learned during the research preview. We heard three things loud and clear:People needed the connectors to work better. The strongest reactions came through Claude and ChatGPT. So we prioritized ChatGPT support for GA and made the MCP experience seamless. If you want to query your library, your chat interface should be the last friction point, not the first.Builders needed output they could control. Developers told us a black-box "final edit" wasn't what they wanted. They needed structured clips, JSON, artifacts they could manipulate. Creators and marketers kept asking us: "Why is this video trending? What specific hooks are holding attention? What common patterns make these reels go viral?" We listened, and built social intelligence features that analyze video hooks, breakdown visual and audio pacing, and explain what actually works across trending content. We also added social ingestion of URL links from YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram Reels, so users can analyze what's working in the wild and search performance alongside content without having to upload videos. It's a whole new way to deconstruct viral video performance.Library-level understanding is the point. You point Jockey at thousands of videos and images, and it reasons across all of them, not just one. That's why we built it this way, and why every model upgrade makes it better without you lifting a finger.If you're building a video app, organizing footage, or trying to find something in thousands of hours of content, Jockey is for you. week.description: Talanoa is your first email messenger. It turns messy email threads into clean, chat-like conversations, removing quotes, signatures and clutter along the way. comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋 I’m John, the solo maker behind Talanoa. Funny enough, Talanoa was never supposed to become a product. I originally built it just for myself. I spend a huge part of my day in email, but I never really liked using traditional email clients. So instead of looking for yet another one, I started building the inbox I wanted for myself. Then I showed it to a few friends. They loved it. They started using it. And eventually, they put enough pressure on me to turn my little personal project into a real product. So… here we are. Along the way, one idea became increasingly obvious to me: Email is a conversation that forgot it was one. A thread between two people is basically a chat. A message, a reply, a reply to the reply. Yet email clients still show repeated quotes, signatures, headers, footers and years of clutter. So I rebuilt Talanoa around a different idea: what if email felt more like a messenger? Today, Talanoa turns your inbox into clean, chat-like conversations, while keeping everything that makes email, email. But it goes further: 💬 Emails become actual conversations ✅ Any email can become a todo with a next step and due date 📅 Your calendar lives alongside your conversations ✨ AI helps you search, summarize and write, entirely on-device 📥 Gmail, Outlook, iCloud and IMAP accounts can live in one inbox 🔒 No cloud sync, no tracking. Your emails stay on your computer. I’ve been building Talanoa independently, talking to users, breaking things, rebuilding them, and questioning quite a few assumptions we’ve had about email for the last 30 years. What started as a tool I built for myself has slowly become something much bigger, and this version finally feels like the Talanoa I always wanted to use. I’d genuinely love your feedback, especially on one thing: Does the “email as a conversation” approach change the way you feel about your inbox? week.name: Google EmbeddingGemma 2
week.tagline: An open, lightweight multimodal embedding model
week.description: EmbeddingGemma 2 is Google DeepMind's open embedding model that maps text, code, images, video and audio into one shared space, so you can search across them from a single query. At 740M parameters it runs on-device, needing about 567MB of RAM on a Pixel 11 Pro for the full multimodal model (191MB for text only). Apache 2.0 licensed, with weights on Hugging Face and Kaggle. MTEB Code score rises from 68.76 to 78.68.

comments.text: EmbeddingGemma 2 is Google DeepMind's open, lightweight multimodal embedding model. It maps text, code, images, video and audio into one shared space and is small enough to run on a phone.Problem: Searching by meaning usually needs a pipeline of separate models: a captioning model for images, speech-to-text for audio, a text embedder on top. That's slow, memory-hungry, and often sends your data to the cloud. For private, on-device apps, that's a hard trade-off.Solution: One 740M-parameter model, built on the Gemma 4 architecture, that embeds all five types of content in the same space. A text query can find a photo, and a voice memo can find a video clip. Everything runs locally, so your data never has to leave the device.What makes it different: It's modular. You can load only the encoders you need, as little as 270M parameters for text and code, plus optional vision (170M) and audio (300M) encoders. With quantization on a Pixel 11 Pro, it needs about 191MB of RAM for text only and about 567MB for the full multimodal model. It shares its tokenizer and audio encoder with Gemma 4, so running both together uses less memory than running them separately.Key features:Text, code, images, video and audio in a single embedding space8K token context (4x EmbeddingGemma 1), enough for about 5.5 minutes of audio, 29 images or 58 video framesVectors can be shrunk from 768 to 512, 256 or 128 dimensions for up to 6x less storageCode retrieval improves from 68.76 to 78.68 on MTEB Code (+9.92 points)Google says it leads sub-1B multimodal embedding models on benchmarks like MTEB Code and MAEB (audio)Can also act as a zero-shot, on-device decision engine: Google's MediaPipe demo scores 500 options per turn in a chess game in under 100 msWorks with transformers, sentence-transformers, MLX, vLLM, llama.cpp, SGLang, Ollama, LMStudio, Qdrant and UnslothWho it's for: Developers building private, offline-capable search, RAG, media retrieval or local codebase search, and anyone who wants cross-modal search without a cloud dependency. P.S. I hunt the latest and greatest launches in tech, SaaS and AI, follow to be notified → @rohanrecommends

month.name: Rill Browser

month.description: Rill is an AI-native browser built around the Claude Code and Codex you already use. Full disclosure — I'm a big fan of Anthropic and actually built an app that works exclusively with Claude Desktop for secure local file search. So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.
